sections.markdown:
## D — Collision avoidance and emergencies

Accuracy scope: every fact in Collision avoidance and emergencies uses one physical page of the registered Kansas handbook, with original wording and one complete claim per block.
All quantities and exceptions are edition-bound. The cited handbook is the evidence; no recollection or competitor text supplies authority.
Source flags: ABS guarantees, collision-airbag guarantees, rollover statistics, night headlight-speed examples and a cross-section following-interval conflict are not converted into unqualified facts. Mechanical-control instructions retain their described equipment context. [A73] [A74] [A75] [A76] [A77] [A78]
Refresh disposition: legal thresholds and administrative procedures require rechecking against an issuer source when a later edition replaces this snapshot.

corpus_stability.reason: The bound Kansas handbook has one February 2022 revision label; the selected source contains no evidence of multiple annual corpus rewrites. Later legal or administrative changes require issuer rechecking.

verification_debt.claim_text: Page 73 L14-19 says ABS allows a stop without skidding and only works with the pedal fully depressed. The absolute equipment guarantee is not established across vehicles and traction conditions; the hard-stop procedure and owner's-manual instruction are retained without a universal guarantee.

Page 74 L45-55 says frontal airbags will not help in a side strike, a severe front impact will deploy the airbag, and an attempted turn yields at worst a glancing blow. Vehicle-specific response and collision outcomes are not guaranteed; withhold these absolutes pending issuer/vehicle documentation.

Page 76 L20-31 gives about one in forty police-reported-crash vehicles rolling over, one in three passenger-occupant deaths in rollovers, and more than 80 percent single-vehicle involvement in rollovers. Study date, population and provenance are absent; retain all three values as unverified statistical debt rather than current risk rates.

Page 77 L9-17 pairs low-beam 150-200-foot visibility with about 45 mph and high-beam 350-400 feet with about 65 mph. Stopping, vehicle and road assumptions are unstated; do not teach these as guaranteed safe speeds. The stop-within-visible-distance rule is supported.

Page 77 L36-38 gives a minimum three-second interval with an extra second for unusual weather/traffic, whereas page 62 L45-49 gives two seconds plus an extra second. No distinct general context reconciles the minima. Preserve both values and leave the universal numeric rule unresolved; do not edit section07 accepted history.
